alignment.note: Greek uses the articular subject with postpositive δέ (ὁ δέ, 'but he'); the Vulgate renders this adversative-resumptive with At ille, idiomatically capturing the same nominative pronoun-plus-connective. The Peshitta omits any explicit subject pronoun and connective, expressing the subject only through the verbal inflection.

Greek and Latin both attest the participle of answering (ἀποκριθείς / respondens), a Semitic-style pleonastic verb of replying. The Peshitta lacks any equivalent of 'answering', collapsing the response to the single verb 'he said'.

The dative 'to them' (αὐτοῖς / ܠܗܘܢ / eis) is shared by all three; the Greek attaches a raised dot and the Vulgate sets off a separate colon token introducing direct discourse, a punctuation feature absent in the unpointed Peshitta.

Greek and Latin express the indirect object as a separate enclitic/pronoun (ὑμῖν / vobis); the Peshitta incorporates the second-person plural object as a pronominal suffix on the verb (ܦܩܕܟܘܢ), so it is aligned within the verb group rather than standing alone.
